params.body:
## What

The sequel to `what-we-have.md` (#196). That note says what we hold; this says who may see which part of it, through which surface, and what opening each one costs us.

It exists because Maarten wants to offer the underlying layers to enterprise, and six surfaces are six chances for the same word to mean six things. A sales conversation needs a floor that does not move.

## What it says

**One ladder, six depths.** A surface is not an application, it is a cut through the ladder (signal, concept, pattern, insight, piece) at a chosen depth for a chosen reader. The table names all six with how deep each reaches and whether it is built: Observatory and Studio for us, Explorer and Editorial for customers, Assist not built, and the door for machines.

**The door is not a sixth peer.** It is a second form of the other five. Treated as a peer it grows its own vocabulary and drifts; treated as a form, every ability that exists gets a machine shape for free and `whoami` tells the agent which ones its key holds. That is how it works today and the note says to keep it that way.

**A rule for where a new feature belongs.** Ask how deep down the ladder it reaches. A feature that needs a prompt belongs to the Observatory and nowhere else; one that needs a signal url belongs to the Explorer at the plan that opens sources. A feature that seems to belong to two surfaces is two features.

**One-way dependency.** Every surface reads the layer under it and none reaches around it. The deepest enterprise plan still reads through the same gate: no database login, no export door, no second writer. The site already works this way as a projection, and that is the decision that keeps this from becoming six systems.

**What each surface costs to open**, since the cost is the same whether we charge for it or not. Most of the brakes already exist (seven abilities, per-key and per-account allowances, a quarter of the catalogue a day, OAuth and metering, the tenant boundary in CI). The Observatory stays internal, and the note says why in a form that can be said out loud to a customer: opening it converts an internal instrument into a product with obligations, and those are paid in the freedom to change it.

**Two graphs, one method**, and the three on-premise roads, of which only two are defensible.

**Three depths of one object**, so the easy path and the deep path stay the same thing.

## What it asks for next

Name the Explorer, build Assist at depth one against the boundary that already exists, add a consent record before the second customer brings anything, and let a measurement name the reading it was computed under.

Nothing is built by this PR.
params.title: The surfaces: one ladder, six depths, and what each costs to open
